subject: Uptime attestation, alert routing, and metrics access for procurement questionnaire
messages:
From: Dana Lee <dana.lee@cloudbank.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudbank.com, Samuel Park <samuel.park@cloudbank.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement questionnaire: measurement methodology for uptime & latency

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this — our procurement team sent over the attached questionnaire and a couple of follow-up questions about how Redwood measures uptime and latency for customer-facing endpoints. Two quick items they flagged:

1) Measurement windows and sampling: procurement wants to confirm whether you report p95/p99 over rolling 30d windows or calendar months, and what sampling (synthetic vs. production telemetry) is used.
2) Dashboard/access: they asked if CloudBank can get read-only access to the production metrics dashboard (or a one-way feed) and whether alert notifications can be routed to our PagerDuty integration for incident correlation.

We attached the questionnaire as a PDF and added a few inline questions below. Could you confirm by EOD Wednesday? We have a vendor review meeting next Friday.

Questions (procurement):
- Do uptime figures include scheduled maintenance windows? If yes, what's the notice period and how are exceptions applied?
- For latency SLAs, do you use synthetic probes, client-perceived latency, or server-side histograms?
- If CloudBank needs a temporary access carve-out for a small set of dashboards, what is the access model and data retention limits?

Appreciate your help — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Dana Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
CloudBank

Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: measurement methodology for uptime & latency

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together answers below and looped in Karthik for instrumentation specifics and Marissa for the contractual carve-outs. High level: we measure both synthetic and production telemetry, provide time-windowed aggregates (rolling 30d by default), and can offer a read-only dashboard view or push metrics to a customer-managed endpoint with a retention policy.

Summary answers:
- Windows: p95/p99 are calculated over a rolling 30-day window by default; calendar-month aggregation available on request.
- Sampling: primary SLA calculations use server-side production histograms (full sampling), augmented by synthetic checks for availability.
- Scheduled maintenance: planned maintenance windows are excluded from uptime calculations if communicated 72 hours in advance; emergency maintenance follows an exception process documented below.
- Dashboard/access: we can grant CloudBank read-only access to a tenant-scoped Grafana dashboard, or provide a metrics push (Prometheus remote_write) to a customer endpoint for SRE ingestion.

I left Karthik to add instrumentation specifics (histogram buckets, edge vs. core checks), and Marissa to confirm how we'd reflect any short-term exceptions in the SLA annex.

Next steps: Karthik will upload a short instrumentation workbook and Marissa will draft the annex language for the procurement team to review. Happy to schedule a 30-minute sync if you prefer.

Best,
Avery Johnson

Hi Dana — adding instrumentation detail as requested and attaching a short XLSX that maps metrics to the SLA math. I'm keeping this at an observer-friendly level.

Instrumentation & measurement notes:
- Primary sources: server-side request histograms (per-region), API gateway ingress logs, and per-model worker metrics. We compute latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) from production histograms with 10ms resolution buckets up to 2s, then 50ms buckets to 10s.
- Aggregation windows: rolling 30d by default. For audit purposes we store raw histograms for 90 days; aggregates are retained for 24 months. Calendar-month reports are available as an export.
- Availability measurement: synthetic probes from three regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) executed every 30s against tenant-scoped endpoints. Synthetic checks are used to detect regional degradations quickly but are not the single source of truth for SLA math — production success rate is.
- Maintenance and exceptions: planned maintenance with >=72h notice is excluded from uptime math. Emergency maintenance or force-majeure events follow our exception review process: Redwood provides a written incident summary within 48h and a remediation timeline; procurement teams may request a temporary carve-out which must be recorded in the SLA annex.
- Alerting & routing: we can forward operational alerts (severity >= page) to CloudBank's PagerDuty integration via a dedicated integration key. Alert deduplication and notification throttling policies are configurable per integration. For change control, we require a single integration contact and an RBAC list to be provided by CloudBank.
- Dashboard access: we provide a tenant-scoped Grafana stack with read-only org role for customers; sensitive traces and raw logs remain Redwoods-internal unless a data-sharing agreement is in place. Alternatively, we offer a push model (Prometheus remote_write) to a customer-managed ingestion endpoint — this approach gives CloudBank full ownership of retention and alerting.

Attachments: SLO-instrumentation-summary.xlsx (maps metric names to telemetry sources, retention, and compute method); Redwood_SLO_Definitions_v1.pdf (human-readable definitions).

If procurement wants a one-page exhibit listing exact wording for "excluded events" and "maintenance windows," Marissa and I can draft it and include an example calculation for p99 uplift during a planned canary.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Observability & Instrumentation
Redwood Inference

- SRE requests a short-lived (30-day) read-only Grafana invite scoped to synthetic+latency dashboards to validate the sampling approach. We can provide a list of reviewer emails.
